extracted.intended_audience: members of the Canadian Mathematical Society, mathematicians, teachers, students, and potential authors for CMS publications
extracted.subtask_description: A society web page listing the Canadian Mathematical Society's journals, book series, problem-solving periodicals, newsletters, and related publication channels, with short descriptions and submission/contact pointers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Journals (CJM, CMB, CMC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Journals: Canadian Journal of Mathematics (CJM); Canadian Mathematical Bulletin (CMB); Canadian Mathematical Communications (CMC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the society's research-level journal outlets for mathematical research (page lists them under 'Research Journals'). No further submission criteria are given on this page; consult each journal's own pages for author guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly Book Series (CMS/CAIMS Books in Mathematics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly Book Series: CMS/CAIMS Books in Mathematics (published by Springer). Successor to the CMS Books in Mathematics series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the society's scholarly book series and publisher; for book proposals/submissions consult the specific series' instructions (not detailed on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crux Mathematicorum (CRUX) — target audience & scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Crux Mathematicorum (CRUX) – Since 1975, this professionally-published periodical has been an internationally respected source of unique and challenging mathematical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed primarily for the secondary and undergraduate levels, and also containing some pre-secondary material. Described as 'the best problem solving journal in the world'. Free online. Ten issues per year. Use this outlet for challenging problem-solving material aimed at those education levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: A‑Taste‑Of‑Mathematics (ATOM) — intended content & audience
rubrics_metrics.description: A-Taste-Of-Mathematics (ATOM) – This series of 17 booklets is now freely available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are designed to provide enrichment materials for pre-university students, and their teachers, who have an interest in mathematics. Some booklets cover materials for mathematical competitions at national and international levels, while other booklets cover topics of broad interest to students and teachers such as puzzle collections, applications of mathematics, as well as treatises through a historical, social, or cultural lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS Notes — newsletter scope, content types, and submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS Notes – CMS Notes is the official newsletter of the Canadian Mathematical Society. It features articles on research, education, meetings, book reviews, calendar of events, awards and calls for nominations, news from math departments and institutions and employment opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial team welcomes your comments, suggestions, and submissions. CMS Notes is an online-only publication and is published six times a year (February, March/April, June, September, October/November and December). Please visit the deadlines page to know the date that content submissions are due for each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: MathMatters — frequency and access
rubrics_metrics.description: MathMatters – Weekly compendium of news of interest to the Canadian Mathematical Community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free access. Use this channel for short, timely items of community news.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMath — announcement email list
rubrics_metrics.description: CMath – Announcement email list for the wider Canadian mathematical community (includes MathMatters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for community-wide announcements; subscribe or submit items as appropriate to reach the broader community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction licenses and rights contact
rubrics_metrics.description: For queries regarding reproduction licenses or rights, please contact the managing-editor@cms.math.ca.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural contact guidance for permissions and rights questions related to CMS publications.
